recall_prompt: Say how you would count the functions from a five-element set into a four-element set — how many choices each element has, and the number.
insider_note: The base is the size of the target set: each of the 5 elements of A has 4 choices of image, so the count is 4⁵ = 1024, not 5⁴ = 625. Saying "each element has 4 choices" fixes the base before the slip can happen.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Each element has 4 choices of image
steps.margin_note: First mark. A function gives every element of A one image in B, with no restriction — each of the 5 elements has 4 choices, independently: 4⁵.
lines: Each of the 5 elements of A can have any
of the 4 elements of B as its image.

recall.must_convey: That each of the 5 elements independently has 4 choices of image, so the count is 4 to the power 5.
accept: each element has four choices so it is four to the power five
five elements each with four images, four times four five times
n to the r with n four and r five
prathi element ki four choices, four power five
images can repeat so it is four to the fifth

steps.why: A function has no one-one condition, so images may repeat; the choices for different elements are independent and multiply. The base is the size of B (the choices), the exponent is the size of A (the number of choices made).
common_mistakes: Using ⁴P₅, which does not exist, or ⁵P₄, which counts something else.

steps.label: Evaluate 4⁵

accept: four to the power five is one thousand twenty four
four multiplied five times gives ten twenty four
four power five one thousand twenty four
the answer is one thousand and twenty four

steps.why: The question asks for a number; 4⁵ = 1024 is the same as 2¹⁰, a value worth knowing.
